findings.evidence: PLL requests board input 100 MHz, output1 110 MHz and output2 55 MHz; both generated actual-jitter checks reject >230.0 ps. Both requested phase 0 and duty 50%. Top maps clk_out1 to DUT member0 and clk_out2 to APB member1. Actual generated XCI values are not yet assessed here.

harnessSysPLL/clk_out1 and clk_out2 occur in the same asynchronous-group member; PCIe reference/AXI clocks occupy the other group. No APB-to-DUT clock-group cut or new synchronizer-specific false path appears in the generated SDC. Existing PCIe axi_aresetn, PERST and POR through-exceptions remain. Effective vendor constraints and routed exception coverage still require physical audit.

HBM APB_0_PCLK follows wrangler member1/55 MHz; AXI_00_ACLK follows DUT member0/110 MHz; HBM_REF_CLK_0 follows independent board sys-clock broadcast/100 MHz. HBM IP explicitly requests USER_APB_PCLK_0=55. Actual hard-primitive pins, clocks, waveforms and XCI-derived period remain pending.

pcieResetControl monitorClock is sys_clock_ibufds.O (independent board100). releaseSync asynchronously asserts on rawPllReset OR externalReset, where rawPllReset is !harnessSysPLL.locked OR POR and externalReset is !IBUF(prst_n). The PLL reset input itself is POR only.

Three-stage releaseSync drives qualification; !q asynchronously clears the 14-bit stableCount and released FF. Counter terminal is 14h270F (9999), and released becomes sticky after 10000 healthy monitor-clock counting edges. Earliest qualified output is after three synchronizer edges followed by 10000 counting edges (10003 total); output is q AND released. RTL edge accounting only, not a postroute recovery/removal result.

Guard output AND !POR reaches CustomXDMA.io_clocks_sys_rst_n then nm37_xdma.blackbox.sys_rst_n. Guard uses board clock plus pre-wrangler PLL/POR/PERST causes, never wrangler output nor HBM completion. Wrangler may wait for XDMA axi_aresetn, but guard does not wait for wrangler. Guard output never drives PLL reset, so the reviewed startup dependency is acyclic.

Each HBMAsyncLevelSynchronizer declares reg[2:0] sync initialized 000, ASYNC_REG=TRUE and SHREG_EXTRACT=NO, asynchronously cleared and shifted {sync[1:0],d}. Instances are pcieResetControl/releaseSync plus dutDomain/ram_startup/{apbResetN_apbResetSync,axiResetN_axiResetSync,completeAxi_completeSync}. These exact emitted instance names match the frozen hbm_audit query names. Preservation as twelve distinct FDCE registers with correct INIT/properties/fanout must be checked after synthesis.

Common reset is OR of wrangled APB and DUT resets. APB reset releases through three APB edges with d=1. AXI reset synchronizer remains asynchronously asserted while common reset OR !apbResetN is true, then releases through three AXI edges. HBM PRESET_N and ARESET_N connect to these local outputs. No completion-dependent reset feedback exists.

HBM apb_complete_0 is connected, first registered as completeApb in the APB domain/reset, then crosses through completeAxi_completeSync in AXI domain/reset. started and fault are AXI registers; started sticks after completion, fault sticks on subsequent lost completion. trafficReady is axiResetN AND started AND completeAxi AND !fault. A fault blocks traffic without reasserting HBM reset or permitting automatic restart; common reset clears state.

All AW/W/B/AR/R valid-ready handshake signals in both directions are ANDed with trafficReady; payloads are direct wires, and the gate adds no registers. Dynamic handshake verification is recorded separately by the sealed hbm-startup stage, not re-run by this manual RTL review.

Wrangler debounce compares its 13-bit counter with 13h157C=5500 and clocks debounce/deglitch from APB member1. Thus the programmed count remains nominally100us at55MHz. Existing three reset catchers follow DUT, APB and PCIe clocks respectively.
